prompt_md: Twelve people sit around a round table, each a knight (always truthful) or a liar. Each one says "both my neighbors are liars". What's the fewest knights possible?
prompt_short: 12 at a round table each say "both my neighbors lie". Fewest knights?
hint_md: A liar only needs one knight beside them for their claim to be false.
explain_intuition_md: Alternating knight, liar gives 6 knights and works, so 6 is the tempting answer. But a liar only needs one knight neighbor to be lying, and two liars can sit together. Repeating knight, liar, liar around the table works with just 4.
explain_math_md: Knights sit apart, and each knight can be the needed neighbor for at most $2$ liars: $$2K \ge 12 - K \Rightarrow K \ge 4$$
